label: The Great Pyramid
title: This Pyramid Was the Tallest Building for 3,800 Years! 🏜️ #shorts
script: Imagine a building so tall that nothing beat it for almost 3,800 years! That's the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt. It was built about 4,500 years ago for a pharaoh named Khufu. Workers used around 2.3 million stone blocks, and some weigh more than an elephant! Its sides line up almost perfectly with north, south, east, and west. And nobody knows for sure exactly how they did it. Which ancient wonder should I visit next? Tell me in the comments!
desc: The Great Pyramid of Giza was the tallest human-made structure on Earth for almost 3,800 years. Built about 4,500 years ago for Pharaoh Khufu from around 2.3 million stone blocks.

label: Stonehenge
title: These Giant Stones Traveled 150 Miles... 5,000 Years Ago! 🪨 #shorts
script: Some of these giant stones traveled about 150 miles to get here, more than 4,000 years ago! This is Stonehenge in England. People started building it around 5,000 years ago. The smaller bluestones came all the way from the hills of Wales. On the longest day of summer, the sun rises right near a special stone called the Heel Stone. Was it a calendar? A temple? A place of healing? Scientists are still arguing! Follow for more ancient mysteries!
desc: Stonehenge in England was begun around 5,000 years ago. Its bluestones were moved about 150 miles from Wales, and the monument lines up with the summer solstice sunrise.

label: The Great Wall of China
title: Can You See the Great Wall From Space? 🚀 #shorts
script: Can you really see the Great Wall of China from space? Nope, that's a myth! But it's still super amazing. If you add up all its parts, it's more than 20,000 kilometers long. That's longer than half the way around the Earth! People built it over many hundreds of years to protect China from invaders. Soldiers sent smoke and fire signals from tower to tower to pass messages fast. Builders even mixed sticky rice into the mortar to make it stronger! Follow for more!
desc: The Great Wall of China is not visible from space with the naked eye — but all its sections together stretch more than 20,000 km. Builders even used sticky rice mortar!

label: Easter Island Heads
title: The Easter Island Heads Have Hidden BODIES! 🗿 #shorts
script: These giant heads on Easter Island have a secret. Many of them have bodies hidden underground! There are nearly 1,000 of these statues, called moai. The Rapa Nui people carved them from volcanic rock hundreds of years ago. Some are taller than a two-story house, and the biggest weigh as much as ten elephants! But how did they move them without wheels? One idea is that they walked them, rocking the statues side to side with ropes! Follow for more ancient secrets!
desc: Easter Island's moai statues often have bodies buried beneath the ground. The Rapa Nui people carved nearly 1,000 of them from volcanic rock — and may have 'walked' them with ropes.

label: The Colosseum
title: The Colosseum Had Secret Elevators! 🏛️ #shorts
script: Almost 2,000 years ago, about 50,000 people could fit inside this giant stadium! It's the Colosseum in Rome. It opened in the year 80, and crowds came to watch shows and gladiator fights. It even had a huge cloth roof that sailors pulled over the seats to block the sun. Under the floor were tunnels and elevators that lifted animals up into the arena by surprise! Some historians think they once flooded it for pretend sea battles. Follow for more!
desc: Rome's Colosseum opened in AD 80 and held around 50,000 people. It had a giant sailcloth roof and underground elevators that lifted animals into the arena.

label: Petra, the Rose City
title: A Whole City Carved Into a Mountain! ⛰️ #shorts
script: What if a whole city was carved right into the side of a mountain? Meet Petra in Jordan! More than 2,000 years ago, the Nabataean people carved temples and tombs straight out of pink rock. That's why it's called the Rose City. They were also water geniuses, building channels to catch the rare desert rain. For hundreds of years, the outside world forgot about it, until a traveler rediscovered it in 1812. Would you explore it? Follow for more!
desc: Petra in Jordan was carved into rose-colored rock by the Nabataeans more than 2,000 years ago — and was rediscovered by the Western world in 1812.

label: Machu Picchu
title: The City the Spanish Never Found ☁️ #shorts
script: High in the clouds of Peru sits a city the Spanish never found! This is Machu Picchu, built by the Inca around 600 years ago. It's almost 2,500 meters up in the mountains. The Inca cut stones so carefully that they fit together without any cement. In the best walls, you can't even slide a piece of paper between them! These walls were built to wiggle during earthquakes instead of falling down. The world learned about it in 1911. Follow for more amazing places!
desc: Machu Picchu, built by the Inca about 600 years ago high in Peru's mountains, was never found by the Spanish. Its mortar-free stone walls survive earthquakes.

label: Chichén Itzá
title: A Shadow Snake Slides Down This Pyramid! 🐍 #shorts
script: Twice a year, a giant shadow snake slides down this pyramid! This is El Castillo at Chichén Itzá in Mexico, built by the Maya. On the spring and fall equinox, the afternoon sun makes triangle shadows on the stairs that look like a serpent's body. And they end right at a stone snake head at the bottom! The four staircases have 91 steps each. Add the top platform and you get 365, one for every day of the year! Follow for more!
desc: At Chichén Itzá's El Castillo, the equinox sun creates a shadow serpent on the stairs. Its 4 x 91 steps plus the top platform make 365 — one for each day of the year.

label: Lighthouse of Alexandria
title: The Ancient Lighthouse That Was a World Wonder 🔥 #shorts
script: More than 2,000 years ago, one of the tallest buildings in the world was a lighthouse! The Lighthouse of Alexandria in Egypt was about 100 meters tall. At night, a huge fire burned at the top, and mirrors may have helped sailors see it from far away. It was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Earthquakes finally knocked it down, and divers have found some of its giant stones under the sea! Follow for more!
desc: The Lighthouse of Alexandria (the Pharos) stood about 100 m tall and was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Divers have found its stones under the sea.

label: The Parthenon
title: This Temple Has Almost NO Straight Lines! 🏛️ #shorts
script: This ancient temple has a sneaky trick. It has almost no perfectly straight lines! It's the Parthenon in Athens, Greece, built about 2,500 years ago for the goddess Athena. Its columns bulge a tiny bit in the middle and lean slightly inward. Even the floor curves up in the center. Why? Many experts think it was to fool your eyes, so the building looks perfectly straight from far away! Ancient Greek builders were masters of illusion. Follow for more!
desc: The Parthenon in Athens, built about 2,500 years ago for Athena, uses curved floors and bulging, inward-leaning columns — optical tricks to look perfectly straight.

label: Pompeii
title: A City Frozen in Time by a Volcano 🌋 #shorts
script: Almost 2,000 years ago, a whole city was frozen in time, almost overnight! In the year 79, Mount Vesuvius erupted in Italy. Hot ash and rock buried the Roman city of Pompeii. But the ash also protected it. Today, scientists have found streets, paintings, and even loaves of bread still inside an oven! People even left funny writing on the walls, just like graffiti today. Follow for more ancient stories!
desc: In AD 79 Mount Vesuvius buried Pompeii in ash — preserving streets, paintings, wall graffiti and even loaves of bread inside an oven.

label: Leaning Tower of Pisa
title: It Started Leaning Before It Was Even Finished! 😅 #shorts
script: This famous tower started leaning before it was even finished! The Leaning Tower of Pisa in Italy was begun in 1173. When builders reached the third floor, the soft ground underneath began to sink. Wars stopped the work for almost 100 years, which actually gave the ground time to settle. In total, it took about 200 years to complete! Engineers have fixed it so it won't fall, but it still leans about four degrees. Follow for more!
desc: The Leaning Tower of Pisa began tilting during construction because of soft ground. It took about 200 years to finish and still leans about 4 degrees.

label: Angkor Wat
title: The Biggest Religious Building on Earth 🌴 #shorts
script: The biggest religious building on Earth is hiding in the jungle of Cambodia! It's Angkor Wat, built around 900 years ago. It covers an area bigger than 200 soccer fields! Its five towers are shaped like lotus flowers, and the whole temple is surrounded by a giant moat full of water. It's so important that it's even on Cambodia's flag! At sunrise, its reflection in the water looks like magic. Follow for more!
desc: Angkor Wat in Cambodia, built about 900 years ago, is the largest religious monument in the world — bigger than 200 soccer fields — and appears on Cambodia's flag.

label: The Terracotta Army
title: Farmers Digging a Well Found an ARMY! 🪖 #shorts
script: In 1974, farmers digging a well in China found something incredible: an underground army! The Terracotta Army has about 8,000 clay soldiers, plus horses and chariots. They were made more than 2,200 years ago to guard the tomb of China's first emperor, Qin Shi Huang. And here's the coolest part. No two faces look exactly the same! Long ago, they were even painted in bright colors. Follow for more!
desc: In 1974 farmers digging a well discovered the Terracotta Army — about 8,000 clay soldiers made over 2,200 years ago for China's first emperor, Qin Shi Huang.

label: Hanging Gardens of Babylon
title: The Wonder of the World Nobody Can Find 🌿 #shorts
script: It's one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, but nobody knows where it was! The Hanging Gardens of Babylon were said to be terraces full of trees and flowers, growing high above the ground. One story says a king built them for his queen, who missed the green hills of her home. But archaeologists have never found them. Some think they were in a different city, and some think they never existed at all! Follow for more mysteries!
desc: The Hanging Gardens of Babylon are the only one of the Seven Ancient Wonders whose location has never been found. Did they ever exist?

label: Göbekli Tepe
title: Older Than the Pyramids by 6,000 Years! 😱 #shorts
script: This place is older than Stonehenge and the pyramids, by thousands of years! Göbekli Tepe in Turkey was built more than 11,000 years ago. That's before people had farms, writing, or even the wheel! Hunter-gatherers carved huge T-shaped stone pillars, some over five meters tall. They decorated them with foxes, snakes, and wild boars. Scientists think it might be one of the oldest temples in the world. Follow for more!
desc: Göbekli Tepe in Turkey is more than 11,000 years old — built by hunter-gatherers before farming, writing or the wheel, with giant T-shaped pillars carved with animals.

label: The Great Sphinx
title: What Happened to the Sphinx's Nose? 👃 #shorts
script: This giant cat has been guarding the pyramids for about 4,500 years! The Great Sphinx of Egypt has the body of a lion and the head of a person, probably a pharaoh. It was carved out of one huge piece of rock, right from the ground. It's about as long as a jumbo jet! But where's its nose? A popular story blames cannonballs, but old drawings show it was missing long before that. Follow for more!
desc: The Great Sphinx of Giza was carved from a single piece of bedrock about 4,500 years ago and is about as long as a jumbo jet. Its nose was gone long before Napoleon.

label: The Antikythera Mechanism
title: A 2,000-Year-Old Computer Found Under the Sea! ⚙️ #shorts
script: Divers found a 2,000-year-old computer at the bottom of the sea! Around 1901, sponge divers near a Greek island explored an old shipwreck. Inside was a lump of bronze full of tiny gears. Scientists call it the Antikythera mechanism. By turning a handle, ancient Greeks could predict eclipses and follow the Sun, the Moon, and maybe even the planets! Nothing this complicated appears again for over a thousand years. Follow for more!
desc: The Antikythera mechanism, found in a Greek shipwreck in the early 1900s, is a 2,000-year-old geared device that predicted eclipses — often called the first computer.

label: The Nazca Lines
title: Giant Drawings You Can Only See From the Sky! 🛩️ #shorts
script: Giant drawings in the desert that you can really only see from the sky! These are the Nazca Lines in Peru, made about 2,000 years ago. There's a monkey, a spider, and a hummingbird almost as long as a football field! People made them by moving dark stones to show the lighter ground underneath. Because it barely ever rains there, they've lasted for centuries. But why make art you can't see from the ground? Follow for more!
desc: Peru's Nazca Lines are giant ground drawings made about 2,000 years ago — including a hummingbird almost as long as a football field — best seen from the air.

label: Mohenjo-daro
title: This 4,500-Year-Old City Had Toilets! 🚽 #shorts
script: 4,500 years ago, this city already had something many places didn't get until much later: toilets and drains! Mohenjo-daro, in today's Pakistan, was one of the biggest cities of its time. Its streets were laid out in a neat grid, like a checkerboard. Many houses had bathrooms, and covered drains carried dirty water away. It even had a giant public pool called the Great Bath! Follow for more!
desc: Mohenjo-daro of the Indus Valley Civilization had grid streets, household bathrooms, covered drains and the Great Bath — about 4,500 years ago.

label: Hagia Sophia
title: The Dome That Seems to Float in the Air ✨ #shorts
script: For almost 1,000 years, this was the biggest cathedral in the world! Hagia Sophia in Istanbul was finished in the year 537. Its giant dome seems to float in the air, because a ring of 40 windows lets light pour in around its base. It has been a church, a mosque, a museum, and now a mosque again. And the people who designed it were mathematicians! Follow for more!
desc: Hagia Sophia in Istanbul, finished in 537, was the world's largest cathedral for nearly 1,000 years. Its dome seems to float on a ring of 40 windows.

label: The Northern Lights
title: Why Does the Sky Dance at Night? 🌌 #shorts
script: Have you ever seen the sky dance? These are the northern lights! They happen when tiny particles from the Sun crash into our air, high above the Earth. That makes the sky glow green, pink, and purple. Long ago, people in Finland told a story about a magical fox running across the snow, sweeping sparks into the sky with its tail! You can see them best near the North Pole in winter. Follow for more!
desc: The northern lights (aurora borealis) glow when particles from the Sun hit Earth's upper atmosphere. In Finnish legend, a fire fox made them with its tail.

label: The Giant's Causeway
title: Did a GIANT Build This Road Across the Sea? 🦶 #shorts
script: Did a giant build this road across the sea? This is the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland, made of about 40,000 stone columns. Most of them have six sides, like a honeycomb! Legend says a giant named Finn McCool built it to cross the sea to Scotland. But scientists say it was made by lava that cooled and cracked, about 60 million years ago! Follow for more!
desc: The Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland has about 40,000 mostly six-sided basalt columns, formed by cooling lava around 60 million years ago — or by the giant Finn McCool!

label: The Green Sahara
title: The Sahara Desert Used to Be GREEN! 🦒 #shorts
script: The biggest hot desert in the world used to be green! Thousands of years ago, the Sahara in Africa had lakes, grass, and rivers. Hippos, giraffes, and crocodiles lived there! We know because people painted them on rock walls, in the middle of what is now desert. About 5,000 years ago, the rains slowly moved away, and the sand took over. Follow for more!
desc: Thousands of years ago the Sahara was green, with lakes, giraffes and hippos — we know from ancient rock art. The rains faded about 5,000 years ago.

label: Mammoths & Pyramids
title: Mammoths Were Alive When the Pyramids Were Built! 🦣 #shorts
script: Here's a crazy fact. Woolly mammoths were still alive when the Great Pyramid was being built! Most mammoths disappeared long ago, but a small group survived on Wrangel Island in the Arctic Ocean. They lived there until about 4,000 years ago! The Great Pyramid was built around 4,500 years ago. So ancient Egyptians and mammoths lived on Earth at the same time! Follow for more!
desc: The last woolly mammoths lived on Wrangel Island until about 4,000 years ago — after the Great Pyramid of Giza was built about 4,500 years ago.

label: The Grand Canyon
title: Walk Through 2 Billion Years of History! 🏞️ #shorts
script: If you hiked to the bottom of this canyon, you'd walk past almost two billion years of Earth's history! The Grand Canyon in the USA is more than a mile deep. The Colorado River carved it, little by little, over millions of years. Each colorful layer of rock is like a page in a history book. Some layers even have fossils of ancient sea creatures! Follow for more!
desc: The Grand Canyon is over a mile deep, carved by the Colorado River. Its rock layers record almost two billion years of Earth's history, including ancient sea fossils.

label: Derinkuyu Underground City
title: He Knocked Down a Wall and Found a Secret City! 🕳️ #shorts
script: In 1963, a man knocked down a wall in his house and found a secret city underground! This is Derinkuyu in Turkey. It goes down about 85 meters, deeper than a 20-story building is tall! Thousands of people could hide there with their animals and food. It had air shafts, wells, and huge round stone doors that rolled shut from the inside. Follow for more!
desc: Derinkuyu in Turkey is an ancient underground city about 85 m deep, rediscovered in 1963 during a home renovation. It had air shafts, wells and rolling stone doors.

label: The Registan, Samarkand
title: The Shining Heart of the Silk Road 🕌 #shorts
script: This square in Samarkand was once a shining heart of the Silk Road! The Registan, in Uzbekistan, is surrounded by three giant madrasas, which are schools covered in sparkling blue tiles. The first one was built about 600 years ago by Ulugh Beg, a ruler who was also an astronomer! He measured the length of a year almost perfectly, without any telescope. Today, the Registan glows with lights at night. Follow for more!
desc: The Registan in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, is framed by three tiled madrasas. The first was built by Ulugh Beg — a ruler and astronomer who measured the year with amazing accuracy.

label: The Taj Mahal
title: The Building That Changes Color! 🤍 #shorts
script: This beautiful building seems to change color during the day! The Taj Mahal in India was built by Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife. About 20,000 workers helped build it, and it took around 20 years. Its white marble looks pinkish in the morning, white at noon, and golden under the moon. Its four towers lean slightly outward, so if an earthquake ever came, they would fall away from the tomb! Follow for more!
desc: The Taj Mahal, built by Shah Jahan with about 20,000 workers over roughly 20 years, seems to change color through the day. Its minarets lean outward for safety.

label: The First Olympics
title: Olympic Winners Didn't Get Gold Medals! 🫒 #shorts
script: The Olympic Games are almost 2,800 years old! The first recorded games happened in 776 BC in Olympia, Greece. At first, there was only one race, a sprint about 192 meters long. Winners didn't get gold medals. They got a crown made of olive leaves! The games were so important that a special truce let athletes and fans travel there safely. Follow for more!
desc: The first recorded Olympic Games were held in 776 BC at Olympia, Greece, with a single sprint race. Winners received an olive wreath, and a truce protected travelers.
